correctness.rationale: The 2-by-2 moment system has determinant \(u(1-e^{i\theta})\ne0\); its solution is exactly \(Q(z)=z^2-(v/u)(1+e^{i\theta})z+ve^{i\theta}\). Phase conjugation produces a real quadratic with \(-1<v<1\), and the strict Schur/Jury test is proved directly. The inequalities \(u\ge\cos\alpha\), \(v\ge\cos(2\alpha)\), and \(|\cos(\theta/2)|<\cos\alpha\) yield unconditional disk roots up to \(\alpha_*=\arccos(1/\sqrt3)\). Endpoint-pair measures give a strict reversed inequality for any \(\alpha>\alpha_*\), preserved under weak approximations by smooth everywhere-interior-positive full-support densities. The endpoint phase equation and uniform-density contrast are proved algebraically. The standalone checker actually passed 14215 supplementary assertions; finite checks are not the proof.

value.rationale: The 2026 Laurent zero-localization theorem draws a clean distinction from the original multiple orthogonality. The present result gives a sharp universal support-width boundary in the very first nontrivial ordinary multiple-orthogonal index, together with exact localized/escaped phase diagrams and smooth full-support counterexamples. The interval of widths is a natural geometric invariant of arc separation, not an arbitrary numerical slice; the uniform-density contrast shows why support information alone ceases to control zeros beyond the boundary.
